citations.assessment: The direct Rosh witness has Shimon ben Yehotzadak, and they ask Tarfon and the sages. Heilprin’s quoted wording has Yehotzadak and Tarfon. Preserve both without harmonizing.

The Bavli directly names R. Shimon ben Yehotzadak as a transmitter for Yochanan and raises whether the report originated with him or his teacher. The title underscores the compiler’s distinction but does not establish distinct individuals.
Semachot’s direct text gives Shimon without the Rabbi title. Those consulted are the sages.
The direct Bavli gives a succession motif including this pair; dates and longevity of Tarfon remain Heilprin’s inference.
The source is Tarfon’s response to Rabban Gamliel about a lone view and a majority. A respectful address does not resolve the identity of Rabbi in the donkey passage.
Direct Bavli gives Rabbi Yehudah Nesia sending the firstborn donkey to Tarfon, and the two parallel texts confirm the name and verb.
The Rosh directly names Rabbi Yehudah Nesia and uses the sending formula.
The Yalkut directly locates the same report and the sending formula.

The Gamliel of Yavneh entry discusses the Berabbi designation and explicitly refers to Tarfon. The local cross-reference clarifies the distinction the compiler is making without establishing a historical identification.
Chapter 6 is the received Yuchasin citation, and Heilprin explicitly corrects it to chapter 4. The link points to 4:11 with the inherited locator visible.

holds.reason: The cited texts preserve their separate accounts. Neither the literal age reconstruction nor the proposed identification with Rabban Gamliel follows from the witnesses.

notes.text: Yuchasin provides the received chapter 6 and the chronological challenge. Semachot 4:11, the compared Rosh and the quoted Rosh have different names and question recipients. citations.assessment: Yuchasin at Abba Shaul infers that Tarfon was his student from the stature comparison. Niddah gives the height rather than direct testimony on study. The local Ramsha entry makes a tentative identification.
Exact Chullin names Oshaya and says he testified before Akiva in Tarfon’s name. The local Oshaya entry describes the alternate form from Tosefta.
Zacuto says that Tarfon appears to have been Meir’s teacher and reads the stature chain as teacher and student throughout.
The Niddah story explicitly measures Tarfon, Meir, and others by the shoulder in sequence. It does not identify those links as pedagogical.
Direct Tosafot says Elazar ben Azaryah preceded Meir substantially and discusses a distinct textual problem. The further argument about Tarfon’s chronology is Heilprin’s inference.
The local Abba Shaul entry gives the stature comparisons, and the separate Ramsha heading explicitly qualifies the author’s identification.
Rava objects on the dimensions of the myrtle and uses the expression asking forgiveness for Tarfon. Preserve context without biographical inference.
The exact Menachot passage describes Shezuri’s question to Tarfon about mixed untithed produce. The reciprocal entry names that and a Jerusalem parallel.

On fresh full-source recheck, Yoma 76a:5 explicitly names Tarfon and Yishmael sitting with the elders, with Elazar HaModai seated among them in the manna discussion. This replaces the provisional qualification in the preceding working packet. The parallel Moed Katan scene is separate.

notes.text: Yoma depicts Tarfon, Yishmael and Elazar HaModai in the same sitting. Exact Oshaya and Shezuri passages give the direction of testimony and question. Yuchasin makes the teaching inferences from stature, and Tosafot supplies Heilprin’s separate chronology argument. Neither supplies an independently established chain of teachers.
